meta.title: An introduction to cost terms and purposes
meta.summary: Cost objects, direct and indirect costs, variable and fixed costs, the three sectors and three inventories, inventoriable and period costs, prime and conversion costs, and how to treat overtime and idle time.

videos.title: Cost objects: direct and indirect
videos.take: Direct costs are traced to a cost object; indirect costs must be allocated

scenes.say: Every cost question starts with: the cost of what? That 'what' is the cost object.
A cost object is anything you want to measure the cost of: a trailer, a product line, a customer, a department, even a project like a new paint booth.

scenes.heading: Cost object: trailer #418
scenes.say: Direct costs can be traced to the cost object in an economically feasible way, like the steel and axles in trailer four-eighteen. Indirect costs can't be traced, so they're allocated, like plant rent and the floor supervisor's salary.

scenes.heading: What decides direct or indirect?
items: Technology: barcodes and sensors make tracing cheap
Operations design: one product per machine is easy
scenes.say: Whether a cost is direct depends on materiality, since tracing a few cents of welding wire isn't worth it; on technology, since barcodes make tracing cheaper; and on how operations are designed.

sub: The supervisor is indirect to a trailer,
scenes.say: And it depends on the cost object. The welding supervisor's salary is indirect to any trailer, but direct to the welding department.

scenes.q: Cost object: one trailer. Which cost is direct?
opts: Custom aluminum side panels for that trailer
scenes.say: Quick check. The cost object is one trailer. Which cost is direct? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's B. The panels can be traced to that trailer. The others are shared and must be allocated.

videos.title: Variable and fixed costs
videos.take: Variable costs change in total with activity; fixed costs don't, so fixed cost per unit changes

scenes.say: Costs can also be classified by how they behave when activity changes. And unit costs can mislead.

scenes.heading: Behavior
scenes.say: A variable cost changes in total in proportion to activity, but stays constant per unit. A fixed cost stays constant in total over a period, so its cost per unit falls as volume rises.

scenes.heading: Robotic welder lease: $12,000 a month
scenes.say: Prairie Gate leases a robotic welder for $12,000 a month. At forty trailers, that's $300 each. At sixty, $200. At eighty, $150. The total never changes.

scenes.big: Don't treat fixed unit costs as variable
scenes.say: The trap: treating a fixed unit cost as if it were variable. Building a forty-first trailer adds no lease cost at all. Use totals, not unit averages, for decisions.
A cost driver is what causes a cost to change: trailers built for steel, labor hours for wages, number of setups for setup costs. Fixed costs have drivers too, but only over the long run.

scenes.q: Steel costs $3,000 per trailer. Production rises from 50 to 60 trailers. What happens?
opts: Total steel cost stays the same
scenes.say: Quick check. Steel costs three thousand dollars per trailer, and production rises from fifty to sixty. What happens? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's C. Steel is variable: ten more trailers add $30,000. The cost per trailer stays the same.

videos.title: Three sectors, three inventories
videos.take: Manufacturers hold direct materials, work-in-process and finished goods inventories

scenes.say: A bank, a hardware store and a trailer factory account for costs differently. The difference is inventory.

scenes.heading: Three sectors
scenes.say: Manufacturers turn materials into products. Merchandisers, like a hardware store, buy and resell goods. Service firms, like banks and law firms, provide services and hold no inventory of products.

scenes.heading: A manufacturer's three inventories
items: Work in process: trailers being built
Finished goods: trailers ready to ship
scenes.say: A manufacturer has three inventories. Direct materials waiting to be used: steel, axles and tires. Work-in-process: trailers that are partly built. And finished goods: completed trailers not yet sold.

scenes.heading: Prairie Gate inventories, December 31
scenes.say: At the end of December, Prairie Gate has $84,000 of materials, $126,000 of work in process and $58,000 of finished trailers: $268,000 of inventory on its balance sheet.
Service firms still need cost accounting: a bank costs each type of account, and a hospital each procedure. They just have no product inventory.

scenes.q: A trailer with a welded frame but no flooring or wiring is in which inventory?
scenes.say: Quick check. A trailer with a welded frame but no floor or wiring sits in which inventory? Pause and pick.

videos.title: Inventoriable and period costs
videos.take: Manufacturing costs are inventoriable and expensed when sold; other costs are period costs, expensed when incurred

scenes.say: When does a cost hit the income statement? It depends on whether it's an inventoriable cost or a period cost.

sub: until sold, then cost of goods sold
scenes.say: Inventoriable costs are all the costs of making a product: materials, labor and factory overhead. They sit on the balance sheet as inventory until the product is sold, then become cost of goods sold.
Period costs are all the other costs: research, design, marketing, distribution, customer service and administration. Under GAAP they're expensed in the period incurred.

scenes.heading: Prairie Gate's costs
scenes.say: Steel and the factory supervisor's salary are inventoriable: they're expensed as cost of goods sold when the trailer is sold. Dealer commissions and office salaries are period costs, expensed right away.
So factory rent is inventoriable, while rent for the sales office is a period cost. If a trailer built in December is still unsold, its share of factory rent waits in finished goods.

scenes.q: Which cost is inventoriable at Prairie Gate?
scenes.say: Quick check. Which cost is inventoriable at Prairie Gate? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's B. The welding robot is used to manufacture trailers, so its depreciation is factory overhead.

videos.title: Prime and conversion costs
videos.take: Prime cost is direct materials plus direct labor; conversion cost is direct labor plus overhead

scenes.say: Manufacturing costs come in three pieces, and two useful combinations.

scenes.heading: Three manufacturing costs
items: Manufacturing overhead: everything else in the factory
scenes.say: Direct materials are materials traced to the product. Direct manufacturing labor is the pay of workers traced to the product, like welders. Manufacturing overhead is every other factory cost: supervisors, utilities, depreciation, supplies.

scenes.heading: Trailer #418
scenes.say: Trailer four-eighteen used $6,200 of direct materials, $2,400 of direct labor and $2,880 of overhead: $11,480 in total.

scenes.heading: Two combinations
scenes.say: Prime cost is direct materials plus direct labor: $8,600. Conversion cost is direct labor plus overhead, the cost of converting materials into a product: $5,280.

sub: some firms combine labor and overhead
scenes.say: As factories automate, direct labor shrinks and overhead grows, so many companies now track just two categories: direct materials and conversion costs. That's how process costing works in Lecture 8.
Quick check. Direct materials five thousand, direct labor eighteen hundred, overhead twenty-two hundred. What's conversion cost? Pause and pick.

videos.title: Overtime premium and idle time
videos.take: Overtime premium and idle time are usually overhead, not direct labor

scenes.say: A welder works overtime and waits for a broken machine. Which part of the paycheck is direct labor?

scenes.heading: Tom's week: $30 an hour
scenes.say: Tom, a welder, earns thirty dollars an hour, time-and-a-half for overtime. He works forty-four hours, four of them overtime, so he's paid $1,380. Two of his hours were idle while the welding robot was down.

scenes.heading: How it's classified
scenes.say: Direct labor is the forty-two productive hours at the regular rate: $1,260. The overtime premium, four hours at fifteen dollars, is $60 of overhead. The idle time, two hours at thirty, is another $60 of overhead.

sub: The job that happened to run late
scenes.say: Why? Overtime usually results from the overall workload, not the trailer that happened to be on the line late in the week. Spreading the premium through overhead keeps job costs fair.

sub: A rush order that causes overtime
scenes.say: The exception: if a customer's rush order caused the overtime, the premium is charged directly to that job.

scenes.q: A worker paid $20 an hour works 45 hours (5 overtime at time-and-a-half), none idle. How much is overtime premium?
scenes.say: Quick check. A worker paid twenty dollars an hour works forty-five hours, five of them overtime at time-and-a-half. How much is overtime premium? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's A. The premium is half the rate, ten dollars, times five hours: $50.

warmup: What did your last cup of coffee 'cost' the café? List every cost you can, then decide which could be traced to your cup.
Beans, cup, milk are direct; rent, espresso machine, barista's time partly. Introduces cost objects and allocation.
acts: Cost object: the welding department. Direct or indirect? (a) Welding supervisor, (b) plant security, (c) welding gas, (d) the CEO's salary.
Fixed overhead is $90,000 a month. Compute fixed cost per trailer at 45, 60 and 75 trailers. Why is a bid using $2,000 per trailer at 45 risky?
$2,000, $1,500, $1,200. At higher volumes the unit fixed cost falls; and for an extra order, fixed costs may not change at all.
Classify: (a) unused axles, (b) trailer waiting for paint, (c) trailer on the lot awaiting pickup, (d) welding wire.
(a) DM. (b) WIP. (c) FG. (d) Indirect materials (overhead supplies, before use).
Inventoriable or period: R&D on a new hitch, factory utilities, sales commissions, depreciation on the paint booth, CFO's salary.
Job: DM $8,000, DL $3,200, MOH applied at 120% of DL. Compute prime, conversion and total cost.
A welder at $28 works 48 hours (8 overtime at time-and-a-half), 3 idle. Classify the pay.
case: A breeder asks Prairie Gate to price a one-off show-cattle trailer. Karen's cost sheet shows: DM $9,400; DL 90 hours × $30 = $2,700 (including a 10-hour overtime premium of $150 because the welders were busy); overhead allocated at $32 per labor hour; and $1,200 'share of marketing and admin'. The plant has spare capacity this month.
Which costs are direct, which indirect?
Correct the labor and overhead classification.
Which costs are inventoriable if the trailer is still on the lot at year-end?
What minimum price covers the extra costs of this order?

DM and DL direct; overhead and admin indirect. Overtime premium $150 belongs in overhead (not caused by this order) unless the breeder demanded a rush. Inventoriable: DM, DL, MOH; marketing/admin is a period cost. Short-run minimum: incremental costs only (DM, DL, any variable overhead), not allocated fixed costs.
exam: Explain why fixed cost per unit can mislead managers and give an example.
Fixed costs are constant in total, so unit fixed cost depends on volume; using it as if variable overstates incremental cost (e.g., $300 lease per trailer at 40 units, but the 41st adds nothing).
Define and compute prime and conversion cost from DM $12,000, DL $4,500, MOH $6,300.
Prime = DM + DL = 16,500; conversion = DL + MOH = 10,800.
outcomes: Distinguish direct and indirect costs for a cost object
Explain variable and fixed cost behavior
Classify overtime premium and idle time
take: Direct costs are traced; indirect costs allocated
Fixed cost per unit changes with volume
Manufacturing costs wait in inventory; others are expensed
Prime = DM + DL; conversion = DL + MOH
Overtime premium and idle time usually go to overhead

ex.q: Cost object: one trailer. Direct or indirect?
ex.why: Direct costs can be traced economically to the trailer.

ex.q: Fixed lease $15,000 a month; 75 trailers built. What is lease cost per trailer?
When output rises, what happens to variable cost per unit?
ex.why: Variable costs are constant per unit and change in total.

ex.q: Match each item to its inventory.
DM $7,000, DL $2,600, overhead $3,100. What is prime cost?
Same job: what is conversion cost?
A worker at $24 an hour works 46 hours (6 overtime at time-and-a-half), 2 of them idle. How much is direct labor?
ex.why: 44 productive hours × $24 = 1,056; the premium (72) and idle time (48) are overhead.
